Subject: Hosted API SLOs: p50/p95 commitments & burst handling

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Brookline's ingestion pipelines should map well to Redwood's hosted API. Before we move to a final PO, procurement asked for a short note outlining the latency commitments you can make for the Hosted API (specifically p50 and p95), how you measure those quantiles (windowing/aggregation), and any temporary exception language you would expect for short-term burst events.

Concretely, can you confirm:
- p50 and p95 targets by region (US / EU)
- measurement window and aggregation (sliding window, epoch length, how we compute the percentiles)
- whether you provide automatic credits or remediation for transient breaches (e.g., holiday or migration bursts)

We've seen vendors propose a 30m rolling window or hourly epochs; procurement prefers granular measurement & explicit carveouts for planned maintenance or migrations. If you can attach a short sample of recent latency measurements for our expected traffic profile that would be super helpful.

Thanks,
Olivia
Senior Product Manager
Brookline AI

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs: p50/p95 commitments & burst handling

Hi Olivia — really glad the demo resonated. Below is a pragmatic framing we use in most Hosted API contracts; happy to adjust to meet Brookline's procurement requirements.

Proposed commitments (US region, per-route):
- p50 <= 120 ms
- p95 <= 480 ms
Measurement & aggregation:
- Primary measurement is a rolling 30-minute window per-region, computed from request-complete latency (end-to-end, excluding initial DNS lookup).
- For contractual reporting we aggregate into daily epochs where a route is considered "in-compliance" for a day if 95% of 30-minute windows across that day meet the p95 target.
- Streaming/long-poll routes measured separately and excluded from token-generation latency metrics.

Burst/exception handling:
- Automatic transient carveout for scheduled maintenance and documented migrations (must be notified 48 hours in advance).
- For unplanned short-duration bursts (under 6 hours), we offer a remediation pathway: a credits schedule tied to severity and duration — default is a 10% usage credit for single-day p95 violations above baseline; larger remediation negotiable for multi-day events.

I've attached a small sample snapshot of recent latency measurements from a similar customer (slo_evidence_snapshot.csv) so you can see distribution shape and typical burst profiles. If procurement wants us to replace the daily-epoch wording with an alternate windowing model (e.g., 1h epoch or weighted rolling quantiles) we can accommodate that in the SLA addendum.

If that looks reasonable, I'll loop in Legal for a short addendum and propose a DocuSign route for the final signature.

Best,

Thanks for the ping. Operationally the targets look achievable for typical text-generation routes on our G5 fleet with standard KV cache enabled — the p95 is conservative and gives us room for transient jitter. A few suggested changes to protect both parties and make the clause auditable:

1) Measurement clarity: keep the 30-minute rolling window but make the contractual metric the weighted daily compliance described below:
   - Compute quantiles on 30m windows per region. For reporting, we compute the fraction of 30m windows in the day that meet p95 target; if fraction >= 95% the day is compliant.
   - Store and retain latency windows and sample IDs for 90 days for audit requests.
2) Bursts: allow two automatic 6-hour burst carveouts per quarter with retroactive notification if the customer can show the burst was tied to a planned migration or a verified third-party outage.
3) Remediation: define a transparent credit table (example: single-day breach => 10% usage credit; multi-day escalation tiers at 20%/30%). Finance must sign off but this is our standard approach.
4) Fallback / graceful degradation: mandate an automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant when p95 is degraded > 20% sustained for 2 hours (this reduces severity and is a measurable operational action).

If you want, I can draft the SLA paragraph and Marissa can attach the sample telemetry we use for audits. Lauren

Lauren Bishop
